why: Replacing the examples taught the model to avoid cutting immediately before complement-introducing words (prepositions/subordinators, 'that', 'how', 'except'), which reduced harmful short-piece cuts (positive gains in the ≤3–≤7 bins) but led it to shift or insert earlier cuts in longer sequences (negative at ≤10/≤99), splitting heads and speaker tags and lowering cohesion there.
lesson: Keep the learned avoidance of cuts before complement openers for short pieces, but avoid overgeneralizing that pattern so cuts are not moved earlier inside subjects, between speaker tags and quotes, or into heads in longer inputs.
